business.title: An adaptive framework for reliability-based topology optimization under multi-source uncertainties
business.description: The lightweight design of continuum structures is essential in engineering, yet their complex service environments inevitably introduce the challenges of multi-source uncertainties. Reliability-Based Topology Optimization (RBTO) methods often face difficulties when addressing these uncertainties, frequently experiencing numerical oscillations under highly nonlinear constraints and exhibiting limited computational efficiency during the search for volume fractions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Particle Swarm Optimization-Adaptive Topology and Reliability Optimization (PSO-ATRO) double-loop framework. The inner loop employs a hybrid PSO-ADMV strategy, which adaptively determines the optimal gradient descent step size to mitigate numerical oscillations during the Most Probable Point (MPP) search process. Simultaneously, the outer loop introduces a surrogate-assisted PSO-MIST strategy to seek the optimal material volume allocation. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated through several numerical examples, including a robotic arm link under stochastic loading. Comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively avoids numerical divergence issues while strictly satisfying the reliability limits, providing application value for the safe and lightweight design of robotic structures operating in complex, uncertain environments.

science.title: A flow simulation method based on digital rock analysis in multi-layer heterogeneous reservoir
science.description: Conventional multi-tube parallel-flooding experiments and single-/double-layer pore network models are insufficient to characterize interlayer interference and microscopic residual oil distribution in thin interbedded heterogeneous reservoirs. This study constructs a triple permeability combined pore network framework from micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) digital rocks. Three digital rock models for high, medium and low permeability fluvial sandstone rhythmic layers are obtained via micro CT scanning and Otsu threshold segmentation, each satisfying Representative Elementary Volume (REV) criteria at 1.2 mm × 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm. Vertically connected three layer digital rock assemblies are built for invasion percolation based quasi steady state two phase imbibition drainage simulation. With a permeability ratio of ~ 3 across layers, permeability is jointly controlled by pore throat size and coordination number, leading to non monotonic variation between mean pore radius and bulk permeability. Reduced permeability narrows the oil water co flow interval; intensified capillary trapping in fine throats dominates this effect, and weakened pore connectivity plays a secondary role. Imbibition exhibits staged flow behaviors: water first occupies large conduits in medium/high permeability layers at low water saturation, and later invades fine pores in low permeability layers, generating layered feature relative permeability curves. Preferential flow occurs in medium and high permeability zones, while irreducible water and residual oil mainly reside in low permeability strata. Under the given permeability contrast, it preliminarily reveals the pore scale control trends of permeability gradients on capillary characteristics and relative permeability evolution. It can provide a microscale simulation reference for waterflooding development of thin interbedded heterogeneous reservoirs. Note that this simulation adopts idealized pore network simplifications under one fixed permeability contrast and mixed wet condition.
